messages.author: 12a8430c1bf3f70b
messages.subject: Re: How to group data
parts:
Hi Samuel,
I'm not clear what your data is or how much you have, but perhaps you might like to plot age on the X-axis and circumference on the Y-axis and then join up the data on each tree with a line and have everything on one plot?

qplot(age, circumference, data=Orange, colour=Tree, geom='path')
or something like that - assuming that the data is ordered by age...
i.e. Orange <- Orange[order(Orange$age),]
This of course will get quite messy if you have a lot of trees

Alternatively you could put each tree on a separate plot using faceting... as long as you don't have too many trees!
qplot(age, circumference, data=Orange, geom='path') + facet_wrap(~Tree)

If you have a lot of trees you might consider grouping them into tens...
Orange$TreeGroup <- Orange$Tree %/% 10
Orange$TreeNo <- Orange$Tree %% 10

qplot(age, circumference, data=Orange, colour=TreeNo, geom='path') + facet_wrap(~TreeGroup)

Lots of possibilities to play with!

Kind regards,
Sean
Dublin

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: How to group data
parts:
Hi:

ggplot() requires data frame input, so the question is whether
nlme::Orange is a data frame:

> str(Orange)
Classes ‘nfnGroupedData’, ‘nfGroupedData’, ‘groupedData’ and
'data.frame': 35 obs. of 3 variables:
$ Tree : Ord.factor w/ 5 levels "3"<"1"<"5"<"2"<..: 2 2 2 2 2
2 2 4 4 4 ...
$ age : num 118 484 664 1004 1231 ...
$ circumference: num 30 58 87 115 120 142 145 33 69 111 ...
- attr(*, "formula")=Class 'formula' length 3 circumference ~ age | Tree
.. ..- attr(*, ".Environment")=<environment: R_EmptyEnv>
- attr(*, "labels")=List of 2
..$ x: chr "Time since December 31, 1968"
..$ y: chr "Trunk circumference"
- attr(*, "units")=List of 2
..$ x: chr "(days)"
..$ y: chr "(mm)"

We see that it is. The 'groupedData' class, as far as ggplot2 is
concerned, is simply a data frame with several additional attributes.
This can be seen as follows:

> orange <- as.data.frame(Orange)
> str(orange)
'data.frame': 35 obs. of 3 variables:
$ Tree : Ord.factor w/ 5 levels "3"<"1"<"5"<"2"<..: 2 2 2 2 2
2 2 4 4 4 ...
$ age : num 118 484 664 1004 1231 ...
$ circumference: num 30 58 87 115 120 142 145 33 69 111 ...

Either form will work with ggplot2. Since the Orange data is about
growth curves, let's plot some:

library(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE)

# To plot the growth curves for each tree, we need
# to use the group aesthetic:
ggplot(Orange, aes(x = age, y = circumference, group = Tree)) +
geom_line(size = 1) +
geom_point()

# To get separate colors for each line, one way is
last_plot() + aes(color = Tree)

The ordering of the tree numbers in the legend comes from the fact
that Tree is an ordered factor.

Dennis
